question: Of the 2256 curve-related incomplete candidates in full original page3 SVG, how many are sourced from explicitly fill-only, stroke-bearing, both-paint, unpainted or unknown paint occurrences? Do the complete rendered shape count and 108 linear cropped candidates match a separate paint walk?
method: Independent XML occurrence walk resolves use references and inherited inline shape style, preserving fill-only curved artwork as possible source glyphs OR filled connectors; carries clip/style uncertainties without interpreting field action. Run on frozen original PDF and SVG, compare v0.2 expansion count, and inventory all >=10pt provisional straight segments in Figure1 crop.

competing_hypotheses.description: Most curve flags are fill-only glyph/vector outlines, not stroke-bearing curves
Some curve flags are stroke-bearing drawn connectors
Some fill-only curved artwork may depict thick drawn connectors rather than glyphs
All curved flags can be safely discarded as irrelevant

falsifiers: Rendered XML shape occurrence count differs from the pinned v0.2 parser's 2354 expansion count.
Frozen PDF, SVG, or 96-DPI raster SHA differs from pinned source.
Any stroke-bearing curve is silently reclassified as fill-only or discarded.
Any fill-only image is asserted to be a verified font glyph without vector-to-raster role reconstruction.
Clip/mask/filter unknowns disappear without independent clipping evaluation.
108 straight-line candidates are called 108 field connector edges or the 2256 curved flags are called distinct physics claims.
An asserted W-to-doublet or g-to-quark action is imported from paper prose as graphical edge or from Woit semantics.
